title: FEET ON THE NECKS OF KINGS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me." So they brought the five kings out of the cave. When they had brought these kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the army commanders who had come with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and placed their feet on their necks. Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Be strong and courageous. This is what the Lord will do to all the enemies you are going to fight." — Josh 10:22-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The five kings are brought out of the cave, and Joshua calls his commanders to place their feet on the necks of these defeated rulers. To our modern eyes this may seem harsh, but in the ancient world it was a vivid, symbolic act. It was a visible lesson for Israel's leaders: these enemies who once terrified you are now completely subdued under God's power. What you feared has been placed beneath your feet.

Notice Joshua's words as he does this: "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Be strong and courageous." These are the very words God had spoken to Joshua at the start of the book. Now Joshua passes that same encouragement on to his commanders. And he gives them a reason: "This is what the Lord will do to all the enemies you are going to fight." The defeat of these five kings was a preview and a pledge of victories still to come.

There is real encouragement in this for us. God often gives us a taste of His power over one struggle so that we can face the next with confidence. Past victories are meant to strengthen us for future battles. What God has done, He can do again.

This scene also whispers of a greater triumph. Scripture promises that one day God will put all enemies "under his feet" — every foe, including death itself, subdued beneath the reign of Christ (1 Cor 15:25-26). The image of enemies beneath the feet points forward to the total, final victory of our Lord. Because He reigns, we can face every remaining battle with the courage Joshua urged: strong, unafraid, trusting the God who subdues every foe.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How can past victories God has given you strengthen you for present battles?
2. What fear do you need to see placed "under God's feet" today?
3. How does the promise of Christ's final victory over every enemy give you courage?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You subdue every enemy. Let the victories You have given me strengthen my courage for what lies ahead, trusting in Christ's final triumph. Amen.
